# Keep Me Secure

> Free, open source MCP server. Ask your coding agent "Is my stack secure?" and it checks every package in your project against public security advisories, then answers yes, no or unknown, with what to do next.

Hosted endpoint: https://mcp.keepmesecure.dev/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no account or token)

Install in Claude Code (needs Node.js 22 or newer; checks by itself each day when you start coding):

```bash
claude plugin install keep-me-secure --marketplace robertkeus/keep-me-secure-mcp
```

Run locally with Docker, in your project:

```bash
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD:/workspace" ghcr.io/robertkeus/keep-me-secure-mcp:latest init
```

## Compared with Dependabot

Use both. Dependabot opens fix pull requests from your default branch on GitHub. Keep Me Secure answers in your coding session on your working copy, and adds flaws in Node.js and PHP themselves, support end dates, platform breaches and OS packages in Dockerfiles. It can also set up Dependabot.

## Tools

- `check_packages` (hosted): checks a list of up to 500 exact package versions
- `check_project` (local): checks every package in the project's lockfiles
- `check_package`: checks one exact package version
- `check_platform`: lists known security incidents at hosting and AI platforms, with what to do
- `check_runtime`: checks a Node.js or PHP version against known flaws
- `suggest_dependabot` (local): returns a Dependabot config with a cooldown that doesn't delay security updates

## Coverage

- Languages: PHP, JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, Java, Kotlin and .NET
- Data: OSV.dev, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list and FIRST EPSS
- Platforms: a curated list of known incidents, at https://keepmesecure.dev/incidents and as JSON at https://keepmesecure.dev/incidents.json. It isn't complete
- Runtimes: Node.js and PHP versions declared in the project, against a curated list at https://keepmesecure.dev/runtimes.json
- Dockerfiles: base image, end-of-life OS, floating tags, root user, and installed OS packages. Exact versions need an image scanner
- Not covered: built images, your servers, software on your computer and your own code
- Test and example folders are skipped by default, and listed in the result

## When it runs

In Claude Code, the plugin runs when a session starts, with a real check once a day per project. A changed lockfile triggers a new check straight away. The hosted URL only checks when you ask, and only what your agent sends.
